description: Branch-form banks (mBank S.A. pobočka, UniCredit Bank CZ&SK pobočka, Fio, J&T) lack confirmed SK-language disclosure hubs.
SK subsidiaries mostly publish annually/semi-annually; quarterly and outlook material for Slovakia exists mainly in parent-group IR (Erste, Intesa, KBC, RBI) and their earnings-call transcripts.
ESEF/XHTML machine-readable filings were observed for Tatra banka and 365.bank but not confirmed for the others; most collection would otherwise be PDF parsing.

Payments-specific disclosure (card volumes, instant payments, POS/acquiring) is not separately searched in this pass — it sits inside annual reports and CSR/sustainability reports rather than in dedicated pages.
Several banks serve documents from hashed or ID-suffixed paths (365.bank /media/{hash}/, primabanka /preview-file/*-NNNN.pdf) that break silently when re-published.

365.bank is mid-transition: KBC announced acquisition of ~98.45% from the J&T side. Its disclosure channel will migrate from J&T Finance Group's annual report to KBC's International Markets/Slovakia quarterly line, and the handover date and treatment (when it enters KBC's Slovakia segment; KBC's 2Q2026 Slovakia result already flags EUR 16m from 'recent acquisitions') were not established.

Regulated-news / ad-hoc disclosure feeds of the parents (Vienna Stock Exchange and OeKB for Erste and RBI, Euronext Brussels/STORI for KBC, Borsa Italiana/eMarket SDIR-Storage for Intesa) were not searched. These carry the legally definitive, timestamped version of results and M&A announcements — often before the IR website is updated.

ESEF/XBRL structured annual filings and Pillar 3 / country-by-country reporting (CRD Art. 89) were not scouted. CBCR is the one parent disclosure that legally mandates a per-country breakout — turnover, profit before tax, tax paid, employees for Slovakia — for every one of Erste, RBI, KBC, Intesa and UniCredit, on a fully comparable basis.

Smaller SK banks with foreign parents were outside the named cell list and were not scouted: mBank (Commerzbank-linked, SK branch), Oberbank AG SK branch, BKS Bank SK, ING Bank N.V. SK branch, Citibank Europe plc SK branch, Fio banka SK, Komercni banka's SK branch, and consumer-finance arms (BNP Paribas Personal Finance/Cetelem, Home Credit SK).

Earnings-call transcripts, Q&A audio/webcasts and analyst pre-consensus were identified as existing (Erste audio/video webcasts, KBC replay webinars and sell-side preconsensus) but not scouted as sources in their own right. Analyst Q&A is where parents are pressed on the Slovak bank levy, mortgage repricing and competitive response — detail absent from written reports.

Parent-language (non-English) IR editions were not scouted: German for Erste/RBI, Italian for Intesa, Dutch for KBC. These sometimes publish earlier, and Italian/Dutch releases occasionally carry subsidiary detail trimmed from the English edition.

TREND (trend.sk) and Hospodárske noviny (hnonline.sk) — the two flagship Slovak business outlets named in this cell — were both left unverified: one refused the fetch, the other returned no search hits.

The payments/technology media channel (Živé.sk and peers) produced no verified URLs, leaving payment-rail news (instant payments, QR schemes, wallets, outages) under-sourced relative to the earnings side.

Per-actor monitoring endpoints were confirmed for only two banks (SITA /firmy-institucie/tatra-banka/, SME /index/tatra-banka). Equivalent tag pages for Slovenská sporiteľňa, VÚB, ČSOB, Prima banka, 365.bank/Poštová banka, mBank and Fio were not enumerated.
TASR and SITA full wire feeds are commercial products; no pricing, feed format or licensing terms were established in this run.

Slovak subsidiaries of foreign groups (Erste/Slovenská sporiteľňa, Intesa/VÚB, RBI/Tatra banka, KBC/ČSOB) are also reported on by Austrian, Italian and Czech media on group results days, and no such outlet was scouted here.

No archival or full-text-search backend for Slovak media (e.g. a press-monitoring/clipping service or a national media archive) was identified, so historical back-runs of earnings commentary are not addressable.
Parent-group (Erste Group, Intesa Sanpaolo, RBI, KBC, UniCredit) analyst material and country-segment reporting on their Slovak subsidiaries was not yet scouted in this pass.
Payments-sector analyst/consultancy coverage of Slovakia (acquirers, PSPs, card schemes, instant payments) is far thinner in the results than banking coverage.
Slovak think tanks and academic/economic-institute analyses of the banking sector (e.g. INESS, IFP/Inštitút finančnej politiky, university economics faculties) were not covered.
Fitch Ratings' actual SK bank-level entity pages were not located directly; coverage was inferred from secondary reporting.
The Slovak Banking Association (Slovenská banková asociácia) own analytical output was not isolated in this pass; results were dominated by NBS.

Public procurement notices of the state financial entities (Úrad pre verejné obstarávanie / Vestník verejného obstarávania) were not searched in this pass, although they are the richest indirect channel for IT, self-service and payments-hardware demand from SZRB, EXIMBANKA and Slovenská konsolidačná.

Other public-interest financial actors were not covered: Slovenská pošta / Poštová banka relationship, Slovenská sporiteľňa's public-sector role, Štátna pokladnica (pokladnica.sk), Agentúra pre riadenie dlhu a likvidity (ARDAL), and the Ministry of Economy's own state vehicles.
Back-catalogue depth was confirmed for EXIMBANKA (reports linked back to 2006) but not established for SZRB, SIH or Slovenská konsolidačná beyond recent years on their own sites.
No Hungarian- or German-language channels were sought; these are unlikely to matter for SK state-entity disclosure but were not tested.

No coverage yet of payment-processing / card-issuing-platform vendors serving SK banks (e.g. OpenWay, BPC/SmartVista, Tieto/TietoEVRY Card Suite, Comtrade, Monet+, Trask, Sofort/Nexi-type processors).
Vendor earnings-call transcripts and investor decks were not mined; SK wins are often mentioned verbally rather than in press releases.
Vendor and bank hiring/partner signals (LinkedIn posts, job ads naming core systems, partner directories) not yet catalogued as indirect sources.
Smaller SK banks and branches of foreign banks (Prima banka, Tatra banka's RBI stack, 365.bank, ČSOB, mBank SK, Fio, Slovenská záručná a rozvojová banka) not yet mapped to named vendors.

The exact RÚZ public API/bulk endpoints and the ekosystém SQL-dump download URLs were referenced in secondary summaries but their concrete endpoint paths and rate/licence conditions were not read from primary documentation in this pass.

Bank-specific supervisory reporting archives (NBS prudential/statistical data warehouse, ECB/EBA data portals mirroring SK institution data) were not covered here; they belong to a supervisory cell but are the natural machine-readable complement to corporate filings.
No LEI-to-IČO crosswalk source was identified for SK financial institutions, which is required to join local register data to GLEIF/ECB/EBA datasets.
Coverage depth of Slovak bank IR domains inside Internet Archive and webdepozit.sk was not measured; it is unknown how many withdrawn annual reports are actually recoverable.

Video/audio archives beyond the TechEvents YouTube channel were not enumerated - individual bank YouTube channels, ITAPA session recordings and podcast formats (where CEOs speak at length) remain unmapped.
Non-bank SK payment actors (PSPs, acquirers, softPOS vendors, e-money institutions) were only reached indirectly via association pages; no member directory was retrieved.
Historical depth is thin: only ~2023-2026 editions of the awards and conferences were surfaced, though Zlata minca runs since 2005 and TREND's awards for 27+ years.
English-language SK event surfaces (international editions, CEE conferences where SK banks speak, e.g. Finweek Kuala Lumpur, FinTech Roadmap) were only lightly covered.

No award-submission documents themselves were located - only nomination lists and result press releases. Submission dossiers (where the richest unpublished numbers would sit) may not be public at all.

This cell yields the filing channel but not the entity list; no consolidated IČO watchlist of SK banks, foreign-bank branches, payment institutions, EMIs and payment agents was assembled in this pass.

Branches of foreign banks (organizačné zložky) and cross-border PSD2 passported providers may have reduced or no standalone filing duty in the SK register, so their SK activity may be invisible in RÚZ.
RÚZ is documented as CC0 and RPO as CC BY 4.0, but the aggregator layers (Slovensko.Digital, FinStat, FOAF) carry their own terms whose commercial-use conditions were not established.
The richest narrative content (výročná správa, poznámky, správa audítora) arrives as PDF attachments; structure and OCR quality across banks were not sampled.
Filings before the 2014 reform were published in the Obchodný vestník / zbierka listín rather than RÚZ; the earliest reliable year of RÚZ coverage for financial-sector entities was not established.

Only the three largest banks (Slovenská sporiteľňa, VÚB, Tatra banka) were mapped to issuer-side disclosure hubs. Smaller regulated issuers likely in scope — Prima banka, 365.bank/Poštová banka, ČSOB SK, UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia (SK branch), Slovenská záručná a rozvojová banka — were not individually verified.

No commercial aggregator of Slovak regulated disclosure (e.g. financial data vendors, Slovak business-intelligence services such as FinStat or Cribis that resell RÚZ/ORSR data) was assessed in this cell.
The CERI search interface's URL/parameter structure, pagination behaviour, and whether issuer filings can be filtered by IČO or LEI were not inspected — only the static documentation pages were read.

Pillar 3 / prudential disclosure (zverejňovanie informácií podľa CRR, 'informácie o banke' under NBS opatrenie) was not scouted, although it is the disclosure stream carrying capital, liquidity and operational-risk detail for SK banks and is legally distinct from Transparency-Directive filings.
Foreign listing venues and foreign OAMs potentially holding disclosure for Slovak bank instruments were not covered (see negative finding on foreign listings).

NBS macroprudential and SREP disclosure stream — O-SII designations, countercyclical capital buffer (proticyklický kapitálový vankúš) decisions, systemic risk buffer, and any published Pillar 2 requirements per institution.
Only 8 of roughly 25-30 SK banks and foreign-bank branches have a located disclosure entry point. Small banks, state-owned SZRB, building societies and EU-passported branches are largely uncovered.

The EBA Pillar 3 Data Hub went live 26 Jan 2026, moving EEA Pillar 3 from per-bank PDFs to centralised structured DPM data. It is unclear which SK institutions are already onboarded and whether banks will keep mirroring PDFs on their own sites.

Coverage is banking-heavy. The payments side of sector=both has only the NBS PSD2/e-money register, because payment and e-money institutions are outside CRR Pillar 3 and have no equivalent prudential disclosure series.

Register účtovných závierok (registeruz.sk), the mandatory Slovak financial-statements register, was not explored despite being the statutory filing destination for FOV, GFI, banks and payment institutions, and having a known open-data API.

English-language Pillar 3 availability is confirmed only for VÚB (parallel _EN PDF series). It is unknown whether Slovenská sporiteľňa, Tatra banka, ČSOB or others publish EN versions, or whether EN coverage exists only at group level (Erste, RBI, KBC).

No URL in this slice has been liveness-verified; several (365.bank disclosure section, the subjekty.nbs.sk PSD2 JSON endpoint, the NBS '/historia/' resolution pages) are inferred from search snippets or path patterns rather than observed directly.
The full roster of SK-licensed inštitúcie elektronických peňazí (including 'IEP v obmedzenom rozsahu' / limited-scope EMIs) has not been extracted.
EEA payment/e-money institutions passporting services INTO Slovakia (a large part of the real SK payments market, e.g. Revolut-type players) were not enumerated.
No IČO-to-RÚZ-entity-id mapping has been built, so licence records and financial filings are not yet joinable.
At least one major actor (Trust Pay, a. s.) reports on a non-calendar fiscal year ending 30 September, which will misalign naive year-over-year comparisons.
MiCA crypto-asset service providers licensed by NBS from 30 Dec 2025 form an adjacent payments-like population that this cell did not enumerate.
NBS/ECB payment statistics (transaction volumes and values by instrument for SK) were not scouted in this pass, though they are the natural denominator for individual PI performance.

First Data legacy estate in SK was only traced as far as the First Data -> SIA Central Europe -> Nexi Central Europe lineage (ICO 31372074). Any residual Fiserv (First Data successor) presence in SK - e.g. Fiserv/Clover distribution or a separate SK entity - was not searched.

Bank-owned/bank-branded acquiring in SK beyond the Erste/SLSP-Global Payments JV was not mapped: Tatra banka, VUB (Intesa), CSOB (KBC), Postova banka/365.bank acceptance offerings and which processor sits behind each.

Public procurement (UVO - Urad pre verejne obstaravanie / vestnik) was not searched. Tenders for card acceptance and POS terminal services by SK public bodies would name bidders, award values and per-transaction pricing.

No conference/industry-event source was harvested for this cell beyond noting ZBK's /podujatia page. Event agendas and speaker lists are a reliable way to discover processors, gateway vendors and terminal OEMs active in SK.

The May 2026 SK QR-payment / notifikacne ucty (NOP) rollout by Financna sprava and major banks was seen only in passing. It is a structural threat/alternative to card acceptance and directly relevant to acquirer and terminal-estate economics in SK.

Slovak-language coverage was achieved for all local actors, registries and media. However, no Hungarian- or Czech-language searching was done, despite Nexi Central Europe running SK from a shared CZ/HU/HR/RS platform - CZ-language disclosure often carries SK-relevant operational detail.
No card-clearing/switching or ATM-network operator for Slovakia was identified in this pass (domestic switch, ATM interchange consortium, or card processor serving SK banks).
The primary Slovak financial-statements register (Register účtovných závierok) was not directly enumerated; only aggregators (FinStat, FinReg) were captured.
The state owner/supervisor of Slovenská pošta (Ministry of Transport, MDV SR) and its shareholder reporting were not covered.
EBA CLEARING STEP2 (to which SIPS is connected) and the EPC scheme participant registers were not enumerated as sources, though they carry SK participant lists.
Only recent report years were surfaced; the multi-year archive index pages for Slovenská pošta and RÚ annual reports were not located, and posta.sk uses hashed file paths.
No confirmed SK-registered BNPL / deferred-payment provider identified; the segment may be entirely served by CZ/EU passported firms.
Individual newsroom URLs for the SK-licensed CASPs (six under MiCA) and for SK-registered AISP/PISP entities were not enumerated one by one in this pass.

Accelerator, incubator and VC portfolio pages (Crowdberry, Zaka VC, Neulogy/Civitta, Sandberg Capital, ESA/Slovak Business Agency) were not systematically mapped, although Crowdberry surfaced as the backer of a SK earned-wage-access fintech.
Social/professional channels (LinkedIn company pages, X/Twitter accounts of SK fintechs, Slovak Fintech Hub cohort announcements on social) not covered.
Hungarian- and Ukrainian-language coverage of fintech actors operating in southern/eastern SK regions was not searched.

The SBA's 14 expert commissions (odborné komisie, 200+ banking specialists, covering payments, security, accounting, regulation, legal) were referenced on /o-nas/ but their individual pages, outputs and membership were not retrieved.
Member directories of ALS SR, FINAS, Slovenská FinTech asociácia, AOCP, SASS, APSÚ, ASINS, SAEC and ITAS were located as URLs but their actual member entities were not extracted in this pass.

English-language association coverage is thin: only SBA (/en/), FINAS (/en/), SAEC (/en/), ITAS (/en/), AmCham and EBF offer EN material. Most position papers, statistics and legislative comments exist in Slovak only.

Employer confederations (Republiková únia zamestnávateľov, AZZZ SR) — which typically include SBA or individual banks and issue tripartite economic positions, e.g. on bank levies — were queried but returned no usable results in this pass.
Compliance/AML and card-scheme-adjacent professional bodies in Slovakia (e.g. a Slovak compliance circle, internal auditors' institute, ACAMS-style chapters) were not searched.

No check was made of whether association press-release and statistics archives are paginated back in time or whether historical PDFs remain reachable (relevant for ALS SR monthly statistics and SBA /novinka/ history).
